# Design and implement the pure difficulty scorer module

## Goal

Deliver the pure TypeScript difficulty library plus its two consumers (gym readout and docs) that satisfies every acceptance criterion of parent work item AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deterministic absolute scorer.** A pure TypeScript module computes a
  **normalised 0–100 difficulty index** for (a) a single `EnemyConfig`
  archetype and (b) a wave (`WaveDefinition`, i.e. one or more groups). It is
  **absolute**: derived only from enemy properties, with no dependency on
  player HP, lives, weapons or power-ups. Same input ⇒ same output; no Phaser
  or browser globals required (runs under Vitest/happy-dom).
- **AC2 — Named, documented factors with a per-factor breakdown.** The score is
  composed from the axes named in the work item plus the data model: enemy
  `count`, `driftSpeed` (movement speed), `shotPattern` (attack pattern /
  accuracy), `fireInterval` (attack speed, inverted), `shotProbability`,
  `bulletSpeed`, `burstCount`, `formationKind`, and Asteroid splitting
  (one large = 7 destroyed enemies across the split chain). Each factor is
  normalised over a documented range; firing factors contribute zero when
  `shotPattern === 'none'`. The module exposes the per-factor contributions
  (not just the total) so a score can be explained. All weights and ranges are
  named constants in one place.
- **AC3 — Monotonicity and independence (unit-tested).** Unit tests assert,
  within the relevant `shotPattern`: increasing `count`, `driftSpeed`,
  `shotProbability`, `bulletSpeed` or `burstCount` never decreases the score;
  decreasing `fireInterval` (faster fire) never decreases the score; a
  `shotPattern === 'none'` archetype's score is independent of all firing
  fields; and wave score increases with group count and mix.
- **AC4 — Campaign calibration regression test.** The computed difficulty of
  the five built-in `LEVELS` is **non-decreasing** in campaign order
  (Entry ≤ Descent ≤ The Core ≤ Firestorm ≤ Predictable Death). This is
  enforced by a dedicated test that uses the real `LEVELS` data, so future
  tuning that inverts the intended curve fails CI.
- **AC5 — Usable by designers in the Enemy Gym.** The `GymEnemies` editor
  panel displays the live archetype difficulty score (0–100) for the currently
  edited `EnemyConfig`, updating whenever a slider/select/colour control
  changes it. The readout has a stable DOM id (matching the existing panel
  selector convention) and is covered by a scene-level test that asserts it
  exists and changes after a field edit. Wave-level scores remain available
  from the library.
- **AC6 — Documentation updated.** The scoring model, factor ranges, weights
  and the recomputed campaign table (all five levels with their scores) are
  documented in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, with the GDD §3.2
  progression cross-referenced. All related documentation is updated to
  reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki
  or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Implementation Sketch

1. Create `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`: exported named constants for factor weights and normalisation ranges, `enemyDifficulty(config)` and `waveDifficulty(wave)` returning `{ score, breakdown }`. No Phaser imports.
2. Create `src/core/enemyDifficulty.test.ts`: per-axis monotonicity, `shotPattern === 'none'` independence, Asteroid split-chain accounting, and wave composition tests.
3. Create `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`: load the real `LEVELS` from `src/waves/Formations.ts` and assert non-decreasing difficulty ordering.
4. Add a live difficulty readout to `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` with a stable DOM id, wired to the scorer and refreshed on every control change.
5. Add a scene test in `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` asserting the readout exists and updates after a field edit.
6. Document the model, factor ranges/weights and recomputed campaign table in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; link the note from `README.md`.

## Key Files

- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` - New pure scorer
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.test.ts` - Unit tests
- `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts` - Campaign regression test

# Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment

## Context

This work item was discovered during planning for AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K (Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive). The Producer confirmed in Q4 that a runtime auto-sequencer is out of scope for the MVP but should be recorded as a follow-up.

discovered-from:AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K

## Relationship

This is a **non-blocking follow-up sibling** of AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K, linked via `discovered-from`. The Producer confirmed (round-3 answer, 2026-09-23) that it must NOT be a blocking child of the parent: the parent's design-time scorer deliverable is complete and the auto-sequencer is deferred future work. It was reparented to top level accordingly.

## Goal

Build a runtime system that dynamically selects and arranges enemies to hit a target difficulty curve, using the difficulty scoring primitive from the parent work item.

## Scope

- Reads the target difficulty curve from a design-time config
- Uses the enemyDifficulty() scorer from the parent work item to evaluate candidate enemy combinations
- Picks enemy groups that best fit each wave target difficulty
- Optionally adjusts counts, spacing, or formation to fine-tune

## Out of scope for now

- Player-state adaptation (adjusting difficulty based on player performance)
- A dedicated UI for tuning the difficulty curve
- Integration with the Enemy Gym editor (the scoring library is the first step)

# Player-death juice parameter model and constants

## Goal
Provide the pure, testable foundation for the player-death "juice": a single
`resolveJuiceParams(severity)` mapping and all tunable constants in one module
(`src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`), so the rendering layers and scene wiring stay thin.

## User story
As a developer/designer tuning feel, I can change shake intensity, flash alpha,
debris/shockwave counts and severity multipliers in one module, and the exported
parameter model is covered by unit tests so tuning does not silently regress.

## Scope
- New module `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` exporting:
  - `PlayerDeathSeverity = 'respawn' | 'fatal'`.
  - `interface PlayerDeathJuiceParams` (shake intensity/duration, flash
    alpha/duration/colour, debris count/lifespan, shockwave radius/duration,
    per-layer enabled flags, particle count/lifespan/scale overrides).
  - `resolveJuiceParams(severity): PlayerDeathJuiceParams` — pure, total,
    deterministic; unknown severity falls back to `'respawn'` (never throws).
  - Exported tunable constants in one module: `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_COLOR`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_COUNT`, `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_LIFESPAN_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_RADIUS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_DURATION_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers, and `PLAYER_DEATH_ENABLE_*` toggles.
- Tests `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` written FIRST (test-first spec).

## Constraints
- Parameter logic is pure: **no Phaser import** in the parameter model.
- Colours centre on `SHIP_COLOR` (0x00ffff) per GDD §7.1.
- Intake assumptions: shake duration ~250–400 ms, intensity ~0.008–0.02,
  flash duration ~120–200 ms; keep values inside those bounds.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ intake brief (AC2, AC4, AC5).
- Predecessor: AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` constants style).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` exists and was written before the implementation; it fails against the pre-change tree.
- [ ] `resolveJuiceParams('respawn')` and `resolveJuiceParams('fatal')` return complete `PlayerDeathJuiceParams` with every field populated.
- [ ] Every asserted `'fatal'` magnitude is strictly greater than the corresponding `'respawn'` magnitude (shake intensity + duration, flash alpha, debris count, shockwave radius).
- [ ] All tunables are exported constants from the single module; no magic numbers remain in the helper.
- [ ] Unknown/invalid severity returns the `'respawn'` parameter set and never throws.
- [ ] `npm test` passes (including the new suite) and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] Covers parent AC5 — severity scaling & no behaviour change: the effect is heavier and every tunable is an exported constant.
data.title: Player-death juice parameter model and constants

Add `playPlayerDestructionSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` — a heavier, layered,
player-specific cue distinct from the generic enemy `playDestructionSound()` —
plus unit tests. Wiring into scenes is a separate task that depends on the
composed juice helper.

the generic enemy pop, so a life lost reads differently from a kill.

# Screen shake and flash layers

## Goal
Add the two highest-impact juice layers — scene-camera shake and a brief
full-screen flash — as thin Phaser rendering helpers in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`,
tracked in a teardown registry and driven by the parameter model.

## User story
As a player, when my ship is destroyed the camera shakes hard and a bright cyan/
white flash frames the screen, so the moment feels weighty and unmistakable.

## Scope
- `applyShake(scene, params)` — calls `scene.cameras.main.shake(durationMs, intensity)` (full 2D); no-op when the layer toggle is off.
- `spawnDeathFlash(scene, params, registry)` — full-screen overlay (Rectangle/Graphics) at configured alpha/colour that fades to 0 over the configured duration, then destroys itself and splices out of the registry; no-op when disabled.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` using `src/test/gameHarness.ts` `bootScene` plus a camera spy.

## Constraints
- No behaviour change to gameplay; cosmetic only.
- Registry contract must mirror the existing `playerExplosions` pattern (`push` on spawn, `splice`/clear on completion and on SHUTDOWN).
- Flash must not block input or swallow pointer events (non-interactive).

## References
- Depends on task "Player-death juice parameter model and constants".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC2, AC4, AC6); GDD §7.1 palette, §7.2 visual style.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Camera spy asserts `shake` is called exactly once with the configured intensity and duration for a `'respawn'` and a `'fatal'` call.
- [ ] The flash is created at the configured alpha/colour, tween duration matches the constant, and it is destroyed and removed from the registry on tween completion.
- [ ] Disabling the shake/flash toggles produces neither a shake call nor a flash object.
- [ ] Existing VFX tests remain green; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Covers parent AC2 — screen shake: a scene-camera shake is triggered on player destruction with configured intensity and duration.

# Debris shards and shockwave ring

## Goal
Add two secondary juice layers that outlive the particle burst briefly — debris
shards and an expanding shockwave ring — each individually toggleable and
teardown-tracked.

## User story
As a player, the explosion reads as a layered event rather than a single puff:
shards fly outward and a ring expands past the ship before fading.

## Scope
- `spawnDeathDebris(scene, x, y, params, registry)` — N small filled shapes in the
  player colour, tweened outward with random directions and fade/shrink, destroyed
  and spliced on completion; seeded RNG option for deterministic tests.
- `spawnDeathShockwave(scene, x, y, params, registry)` — expanding stroked ring
  (Graphics) scaling to `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_RADIUS` over the configured
  duration, fading out, then destroyed and spliced.
- Both no-op when their `PLAYER_DEATH_ENABLE_*` toggle is off.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts`.

## Constraints
- Short-lived only; must not drop FPS or leak per-frame allocations.
- Reuse the existing seeded-PRNG pattern from `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` for
  deterministic tests.
- Colours centre on `SHIP_COLOR`.

## References
- Depends on task "Player-death juice parameter model and constants".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC4, AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Debris count and lifespan match the resolved params; shockwave radius/duration match the resolved params.
- [ ] Each spawned handle is added to the registry on creation and removed + destroyed on completion.
- [ ] Disabled toggles spawn nothing and leave the registry untouched.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Covers parent AC4 — extra juice layers (assumption-marked): at least two additional layers are configurable and individually toggleable.

# Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point

## Goal
Provide the single shared entry point `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(scene, x, y, severity, options?)`
that composes every juice layer (camera shake, dedicated SFX, particle burst,
flash, debris, shockwave) so no scene has to know the layer set, and returns the
handles/registry so teardown can destroy everything.

## User story
As a developer, I call one function with a position and severity and the full
player-death effect plays; each layer is tunable/toggleable in one module and I
cannot accidentally play two sounds or two particle bursts.

## Scope
- `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(scene, x, y, severity, options?)` in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`:
  - resolves params via `resolveJuiceParams`;
  - plays `playPlayerDestructionSound()` exactly once;
  - calls `applyShake`, `spawnDeathFlash`, `spawnDeathDebris`, `spawnDeathShockwave`;
  - delegates particles to the existing `spawnExplosionParticles(scene, x, y, SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE, { patterns: resolvePatterns('player'), registry, ...severityOverrides })`;
  - returns a handle `{ params, registry }` (registry is the caller-owned array).
- `options` allows injecting the registry and a seed for deterministic tests.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` using the scene harness plus spies on the audio module and `spawnExplosionParticles`.

## Constraints
- The generic `playDestructionSound()` must NOT be called by this helper.
- Exactly one particle burst and exactly one dedicated sound per invocation.
- No gameplay state reads/writes; purely cosmetic.
- Keep the existing `_spawnPlayerExplosion` particle call as the particle source
  (the helper delegates) to avoid duplicate spawns when scenes are migrated.

## References
- Depends on the parameter model, dedicated SFX, shake/flash, and debris/shockwave tasks.
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single call produces shake + exactly one dedicated sound call + particles + flash + debris + shockwave.
- [ ] `playDestructionSound()` is not called by the helper (spy assertion).
- [ ] Particles are spawned via `spawnExplosionParticles` with the `'player'` patterns and the caller's registry.
- [ ] The returned registry contains every juice-owned display object and is suitable for SHUTDOWN teardown.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Covers parent AC1 — shared player-death juice helper exists: a reusable helper composes the full effect and both player-death paths use it.
data.title: Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point

# Wire PlayScene lose-life path

## Goal
Route the real-run player death (`PlayScene._loseLife`) through
`spawnPlayerDeathJuice`, using severity `'fatal'` for a run-ending death (final
life/game over) and `'respawn'` otherwise, while leaving the wave-timeout
penalty and shield-absorb paths unchanged.

## User story
As a player, losing my final life feels heavier than a mid-run respawn, and a
life lost in the real run has both the shake, the dedicated boom and the
explosion.

## Scope
- In `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_loseLife(explodeShip)`:
  - when `explodeShip` is true, call `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(this, player.x, player.y, severity, { registry })`
    with `severity = gameState.lives <= 0 ? 'fatal' : 'respawn'`;
  - remove the direct `playDestructionSound()` and `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` calls
    on that path (no double audio/particles);
  - when `explodeShip` is false (wave-timeout penalty, `_timeoutWave()`), keep the
    existing lighter audio behaviour and spawn no shake/flash/debris `[ASSUMPTION]`.
- Leave `tryAbsorbPlayerHit`'s shield-absorb `playDestructionSound()` untouched.
- Add/clear a `playerDeathEffects` registry in `_teardown()`.

## Constraints
- Respawn position, invulnerability duration, blink, lives/score accounting and
  shield absorption are unchanged; no hit-detection changes.
- Event ordering: VFX spawn before the game-over scene transition so `'fatal'`
  juice fires even though `_finishRun` starts `GameOverScene`.

## References
- Depends on "Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC1, AC3, AC5, AC6); AH-0MU3VQ0JR009CSIN (respawn in place).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `'fatal'` severity is chosen when `gameState.lives <= 0`, `'respawn'` otherwise, verified by a test.
- [ ] On the destroy path exactly one dedicated sound plays and the generic `playDestructionSound()` is not called; exactly one particle burst spawns.
- [ ] `_loseLife(false)` (wave timeout) spawns no shake/flash/debris.
- [ ] Shield absorb still plays the generic cue; lives/score/respawn/invuln unchanged.
- [ ] `_teardown()` clears the juice registry; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

# Cross-path regression and teardown sweep

## Goal
Prove the juice is wired consistently across **all** player-hit paths, that the
dedicated sound replaces the generic cue on those paths, and that no scene
leaks juice-owned objects across a stop/restart.

As a developer, I can trust that every player-death path gets the same juice
and that no display object survives a scene restart.

  - `GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()`;
  asserting: camera shake fired once with configured params, dedicated sound
  called exactly once, generic `playDestructionSound()` never called on the
  player path, particle burst spawned once, and every juice handle registered.

# Make the AI config collapsable

## Problem statement

Every gym scene renders a plain-DOM tuning panel (ship config, enemy AI config, boss config) pinned to the bottom-left of the viewport. The enemy AI panel in particular is ~21 rows tall and, even though it is height-capped and scrolls internally, it permanently occupies a large part of the screen and obscures the game view. Designers and testers need to be able to collapse the panel down to a header so they can see the entire screen, then expand it again when they want to tune values.

**Provenance:** migrated from ContextHub work item `WL-0MU1QV98Z004CFBI` (removed there). Original seed text: "In gym scenes the AI config control should be collabsable so that we can see the entire screen."

## Users

- **Game designer / developer** tuning ship/enemy/boss configs in the gym scenes, who needs to toggle the tuning panel out of the way to inspect the full scene, then bring it back without reloading.
- **QA / playtester** verifying gym scenes, who wants the panel collapsed while playing and expanded while editing.

### User stories

- As a designer tuning an enemy in the gym, I want to collapse the AI config panel to a header so I can see the whole scene, and expand it again to continue tuning.
- As a tester, I want a consistent collapse control on every gym panel (Player, Enemies, Boss) so the interaction is predictable.
- As a keyboard-only user, I want to activate the collapse control without a mouse.

## Existing state

- Three gym scenes build a plain-DOM panel that carries the shared `.gym-panel` class (bottom-left anchoring, `max-height: calc(100vh - 120px)`, `overflow-y: auto`, `AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF`):
  - `#gym-config-panel` — `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` (ship config).
  - `#enemy-gym-panel` — `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` (enemy AI config; the tallest).
  - `#boss-gym-panel` — `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` (Central AI boss config).
- There is currently **no** collapse/expand control and no shared panel header/body structure; each scene appends controls directly to the panel element.
- The stylesheet/anchoring contract is regression-tested in `src/style.test.ts`; per-scene tests assert panel DOM ids and `data-config` selectors.
- This is a leaf work item (no children); the AC coverage review returns `proceed`.

## Desired change

Add a single shared, reusable collapse/expand affordance to all three gym panels:

- A shared helper wraps each panel's existing children in a `.gym-panel-body` element and prepends a `.gym-panel-header` containing a native `<button class="gym-panel-toggle">` (with a short title/label and `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`).
- Clicking the toggle flips a `data-collapsed` attribute on the panel; CSS hides `.gym-panel-body` when `data-collapsed="true"`, leaving only the header visible in the bottom-left.
- Panels start **expanded** in every scene; no cross-scene/reload persistence (deliberately deferred).
- All existing DOM ids, `data-config` / `data-config-value` selectors and control DOM order are preserved so current tests and behaviour are unaffected when expanded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Collapse control present on every gym panel, default expanded.** Each of `#gym-config-panel`, `#enemy-gym-panel` and `#boss-gym-panel` renders a header containing a native `<button class="gym-panel-toggle">` with `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` pointing at its `.gym-panel-body`; the panel starts with `data-collapsed="false"` and its controls are visible.
- [ ] **AC2 — Toggle collapses and expands.** Activating the toggle sets `data-collapsed="true"`, sets `aria-expanded="false"` and hides the body; activating it again restores the expanded state. Verified by simulated `click` DOM tests in happy-dom.
- [ ] **AC3 — CSS contract for the collapsed state.** `src/style.css` hides `.gym-panel[data-collapsed="true"] .gym-panel-body` while keeping the `.gym-panel-header` visible, so a collapsed panel shrinks to its header only; regression-tested (computed style) in `src/style.test.ts`. The bottom-left anchoring / `max-height` contract from AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC4 — No regression to existing panel DOM.** Wrapping children in `.gym-panel-body` preserves every existing element id, `data-config` / `data-config-value` selector and control DOM order, and the existing per-scene panel tests continue to pass unchanged where they assert behaviour (selectors updated only where they assumed direct children).
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests, typecheck and build.** New unit tests cover the shared helper (wrap children, toggle state, accessibility attributes), per-scene tests cover the toggle on all three panels, `npm test` passes, and `npm run build` (tsc + vite) succeeds.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated.** `README.md` (gym-panel notes) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.5 document the shared collapse control, its classes/attribute and default-expanded behaviour.

## Constraints

- **No persistence:** the collapsed/expanded state resets to expanded on each scene start (decision Q3 = a). localStorage persistence and a keyboard shortcut are out of scope and should be captured as follow-ups if wanted.
- **Plain DOM only:** the control must work in the existing happy-dom test environment (native `<button>`, no Phaser UI), matching the current panel implementation.
- **Preserve the shared `.gym-panel` contract:** anchoring, `max-height` and internal scrolling from AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF must not change.
- **No new runtime dependencies.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/gymPanel.ts` — **new**: shared `makeCollapsible({ panel, title })` helper plus exported class constants (`gym-panel-header`, `gym-panel-body`, `gym-panel-toggle`) and the `data-collapsed` attribute name; moves existing children into the body and prepends the header/toggle.
- `src/utils/gymPanel.test.ts` — **new**: unit tests for the helper.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — `_buildPanel()` calls the helper (title e.g. "Ship Config").
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — `_buildPanel()` calls the helper (title e.g. "AI Config").
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — `_buildPanel()` calls the helper (title e.g. "Boss Config").
- `src/style.css` — header/toggle styling and `.gym-panel[data-collapsed="true"] .gym-panel-body { display: none; }`.
- `src/style.test.ts` — regression test for the collapsed CSS contract.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — toggle presence/behaviour per scene.
- `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.5 — docs.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Test-breakage risk:** tests that assume panel controls are direct children could break when children are wrapped in `.gym-panel-body`. Mitigation: descendant `querySelector` calls (the dominant pattern) are unaffected; update any direct-child selector to target the body.
- **Discovery risk:** a fully collapsed header must still make the toggle obviously clickable. Mitigation: keep the header visible with a clear label and toggle affordance.
- **Scope-creep risk:** persistence, keyboard shortcuts, animation and "remember last state" are attractive but explicitly out of scope; record them as separate follow-up work items rather than expanding this change.
- **Assumption:** the feature applies to all three gym panels via one shared helper (decision Q1 = a), and the collapsed form is a header bar (decision Q2 = a).

## Related work

- `Enemy design UI covers Gym scene buttons` (AH-0MUAYB7O4009LWBF) — established the shared `.gym-panel` bottom-left anchoring / `max-height` contract this change extends.
- `Gym editor panel with live tuning (Save / Save As)` (AH-0MTHG5BIB006PP0P) — built the `GymEnemies` editor panel.
- `Gym scene sliders bound to live ship config` (AH-0MTA8DMBH007MEHG) and `Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship` (AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V) — built the `GymPlayer` panel.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope: which panels gain the collapse control?** Options: (a) all `.gym-panel` panels; (b) only `#enemy-gym-panel`; (c) only the AI panels (`#enemy-gym-panel` + `#boss-gym-panel`). **Recommended: (a).**
  - **Answer (operator): "1. a"** — all `.gym-panel` panels. Source: interactive reply. Rationale: the shared class makes it one implementation and matches "gym scenes" (plural).
- **Q2 — What does "collapsed" look like?** Options: (a) header bar + toggle button hiding the body; (b) fully hidden panel with a floating "Show config" button; (c) icon-only chip. **Recommended: (a).**
  - **Answer (operator): "2/ a"** — header bar + toggle button. Source: interactive reply. Keeps the panel discoverable and testable via a stable selector while freeing the screen.
- **Q3 — Toggle behaviour and state?** Options: (a) toggle button only, starts expanded, no persistence; (b) toggle + persist collapsed state; (c) toggle + keyboard shortcut + persistence. **Recommended: (a).**
  - **Answer (operator): "3. a"** — toggle button only, default expanded, no persistence. Source: interactive reply. Minimal change satisfying "see the entire screen"; persistence/shortcut deferred.
- **Open items:** none. Intake was initially paused for producer review (comment `AH-C0MUGZF7LN009WJP4`) and resumed once the operator supplied the three answers above.

# Problem statement

The audit runner's parent-first flow re-audits all children on every run because the freshness fingerprint includes the global git HEAD sha. In `--child-in-main-slot` mode, non-interactive runs leave all children with `partial` verdicts, which blocks the parent from recording a "Ready to close: Yes" result even when all parent ACs are met. This prevents audit completion for epics whose children were previously audited.

# Users

- **Audit runner / downtime worker** — expects a non-interactive audit of an epic to produce a valid verdict without requiring a live agent session.
- **Producer / human reviewer** — expects the audit to accurately reflect whether work is ready to close, not to block on stale or unserviced child verdicts.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fingerprint scoping.** `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger; instead it is scoped to child-relevant key files and/or commits so that unrelated HEAD movement on `dev` does not invalidate previously valid child audits.
- **AC2 — In-main-slot partial verdict handling.** When a child's `ac_results` remain `partial` because the invoking agent session never serviced the `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items, the parent audit treats those verdicts as "not assessed" (inherits the child's previously stored verdict or marks them reusable) rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic clarity.** The audit output surfaces a clear, machine-parseable diagnostic that distinguishes a "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" verdict from a genuine "not-ready" child verdict, including the reason code in the audit summary.
- **AC4 — No regression on interactive runs.** The above fixes do not change the behaviour of interactive audit runs (where an agent session *can* service in-main-slot items); those continue to honour the full in-main-slot workflow.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite and confirm zero failures.

# Constraints

- The fix must not introduce a new mode flag or require operator configuration; it should be the default behaviour.
- The fix should be backward-compatible with persisted audit results (old fingerprint format should still be readable).
- The change scope is the audit runner's child freshness logic (`_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`), the in-main-slot verdict accumulation logic (`_build_issue_json`, `all_ac_acceptable`), and the diagnostic output path.

# Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` includes the current git HEAD sha — any new commit on `dev` invalidates every stored child audit.
- In `child_in_main_slot=True` mode, child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking session. In non-interactive runs, these are never serviced and stay `partial`.
- `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect.

# Desired change

1. **Scope the fingerprint**: Replace the global HEAD sha in `_compute_content_fingerprint` with a child-scoped hash (key files + relevant commits).
2. **Handle partial verdicts**: When computing `all_ac_acceptable`, skip children whose verdict is `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot items — treat them as "not assessed" rather than "not accepted."
3. **Add diagnostics**: In the audit summary, emit a reason code or flag indicating when a child's `partial` verdict is due to unserviced in-main-slot items vs. genuine assessment failure.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audit/` or equivalent audit runner module — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`, `_build_issue_json`, in-main-slot verdict handling
- `scripts/audit_runner*` or equivalent — runner invocation, non-interactive path
- Audit output/summary formatter — diagnostic message generation

# Related work

- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic (completed): the parent epic that discovered this issue during audit.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** — Audit parent-first flow (internal assertion): the flow that triggers the re-audit on stale children.
- **SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE** — Audit in-main-slot mode (internal assertion): the mode that creates `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items.

# Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fingerprint scoping is incomplete.** If child-relevant files/commits are not correctly identified, stale audits may still be invalidated or, conversely, genuinely stale audits may be reused. Mitigation: carefully identify the key files that each child audit covers; add a test case that simulates unrelated HEAD movement vs. child-relevant HEAD movement.
- **Risk — inheriting stale child verdicts masks real regressions.** If a child's code changed but the fingerprint didn't catch it, inheriting an old verdict is incorrect. Mitigation: the fingerprint scoping should cover all files relevant to the child audit.
- **Assumption:** all three suggested directions are desired (fingerprint scoping, partial-verdict handling, diagnostic clarity).
- **Assumption:** the audit runner is a Node.js/TypeScript or Python tool within the project; the fix applies to the runner's Python/TS source.

# Intake Brief — Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123)

- **Type:** feature
- **Priority:** medium
- **Status:** in-progress (intake)
- **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

Asteroids are currently placed only as a single fixed formation group in
Level 1 Wave 1. The design calls for asteroids to be a persistent,
escalating roaming hazard: in **every** regular wave of every level, asteroids
should spawn at **random offscreen positions** and drift into the playfield,
with their **frequency growing slowly** as levels and waves progress. This
increases surviving pressure and variety without adding a new enemy archetype.

## Users / user stories

- **As a player**, I want asteroids to appear unpredictably from offscreen
  during every wave so that the playfield always carries a drifting hazard.
- **As a player**, I want the asteroid threat to grow slowly as I progress
  through levels and waves, so difficulty rises without sudden spikes.
- **As a player**, I want variety in asteroid size (more medium rocks early,
  more large rocks later), so the split-chain risk develops over a run.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` implements the E6 Asteroid: constant-velocity
  straight-line drift, four-edge wrap, continuous rotation, three size tiers
  (`large` / `medium` / `small`), split-on-destroy (large→2 medium→2 small),
  never fires. The constructor accepts optional `vx`/`vy` and `sizeTier`.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` places exactly one asteroid via
  `group('asteroid', 'single', 1, { startX: GAME_WIDTH * 0.6, startY: GAME_HEIGHT * 0.25 })`
  in Level 1 Wave 1 only. Every other wave has no asteroids.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` spawns wave groups from
  `WaveManager.planSpawns()`; asteroids roam via
  `Asteroid.updatePosition(dt)`, are shootable during transitions, survive
  wave timeouts, are cleared on boss entry, and are registered with
  `WaveManager.registerDynamicSpawn()` so wave-clear accounting includes them.
  `PlayScene` already exposes an injectable `rng` (`setRng`) and drives the
  simulation through the deterministic public `tick(dt)`.
- `WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS = 30` (`PlayScene.ts`); each wave runs a 30 s
  countdown (`waveTimer`).
- No existing spawn-scheduler module; there is no test for random asteroid
  spawn timings or weight progression.

## Desired change

Add a **random offscreen asteroid spawner** that operates during every
regular wave. It is a pure planner (new `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts`) plus a
small `PlayScene` integration that releases planned spawns as the wave timer
elapses.

### Spawn plan (pure, RNG-injected)

For a given cumulative **global wave index** `g` (0-based across the whole
campaign, incremented once per regular wave):

1. **Per-wave count** starts at `2` and **doubles** each time the large weight
   threshold is reached: `2 → 4 → 8 → …`.
2. **Size weighting** per wave:
   - medium weight is fixed at `80`;
   - large weight starts at `20` and increases by `+20` per wave;
   - when large weight reaches `2 × medium` (i.e. `160`), the weights **reset**
     to `medium 80 / large 20` and the per-wave count doubles.
   - Size tier is drawn per asteroid from these weights (baseline 80:20
     medium:large).
3. **Spawn timing** (fraction of `WAVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS`):
   - `N` asteroids divide the wave into `N` equal segments;
   - anchor for asteroid `i` is `i / N`; a small random jitter (≈ ±5 %) is
     applied and clamped to `[0, 0.95]`;
   - the **first** asteroid is additionally constrained to the first `10 %`
     of the wave;
   - with the baseline `N = 2` this puts the first within 0–10 % and the
     second around 50 %.

### Offscreen origin and drift

- Choose a **random edge** uniformly from top / bottom / left / right.
- Place the asteroid at a random point along that edge, offset **outward**
  (offscreen) by `asteroid half-size + margin` so it is fully outside the
  viewport at spawn.
- Give it an **inward-directed** velocity (perpendicular to the edge, with up
  to ≈ ±30° spread) at the tier's canonical speed, guaranteeing the inward
  component dominates so it enters the playfield promptly.
- `Asteroid.vx`/`vy` continue to drive straight-line motion + four-edge wrap.

### Escalation semantics

- The global wave index is monotonic across the campaign; the large weight
  rises **once per wave**. Under the shipped 5-level campaign
  (2 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 13 waves) the count is `2` for waves 0–6 and `4` for
  waves 7–12, with the weight cycle resetting at the count change.
- Boss encounter: **no** random asteroid spawns (existing boss-entry cleanup
  continues to destroy carried-over asteroids).

### Replacement of the fixed group

- Remove the fixed `group('asteroid', 'single', 1, …)` from Level 1 Wave 1 in
  `Formations.ts`; all asteroids now come from the random spawner. Update the
  existing `WaveManager.test.ts` assertion that Level 1 Wave 1 contains an
  asteroid group.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every regular wave of every level (Levels 1–5) spawns asteroids from the random offscreen spawner; the boss encounter spawns none.
- A wave begins with 2 asteroids by default; every spawned asteroid appears **offscreen** (fully outside the viewport on a random edge) and drifts inward into the playfield.
- Spawn timing: the first asteroid spawns within the first 10 % of the wave window and the second around 50 %; for higher counts spawn times are spread across the wave with randomised jitter and remain ordered/non-duplicated.
- Size weighting: asteroids are large or medium, weighted toward medium (baseline 80:20). The large weight increases by +20 each wave; when it reaches 2× the medium weight, weights reset to 80:20 and the per-wave count doubles (2 → 4 → 8 → …).
- Spawned asteroids are registered with `WaveManager` as dynamic spawns so wave-clear accounting includes them, and existing asteroid behaviours (splitting, timeout survival, transition collidability, boss-entry cleanup) are preserved.
- The fixed asteroid group is removed from Level 1 Wave 1; all asteroids now originate from the spawner.
- Unit tests cover the pure planner deterministically (injected RNG): count progression, weight escalation/reset, timing segments, offscreen edge/position selection, and inward velocity. Integration tests in `PlayScene.test.ts` cover spawn timing against `tick(dt)`, offscreen positions, and boss exclusion.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.1 / §4.2) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§1.2).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Pure logic must remain free of Phaser runtime dependencies so it is
  unit-testable (mirror the `WaveManager` / `Formations` pattern).
- All randomness must flow through the scene's injectable `rng` to keep tests
  deterministic; the planner takes an `rng` parameter.
- Must not spawn while paused or during a wave/level transition, and must not
  break existing asteroid timeout/carry-over or boss-entry cleanup behaviour.
- Keep the spawner tuning in exported constants so it is easy to retune.
- Build → test → commit order only; no `main` branch changes (dev only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — **new** pure planner: weight escalation +
  count doubling, timing segments, offscreen edge/position + inward velocity.
- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.test.ts` — **new** deterministic unit tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — integrate the planner into `tick(dt)`; track
  elapsed wave time and release due spawns; extend `spawnAsteroidAt` (or add a
  helper) to accept velocity; skip paused/transition/boss phases.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — integration tests (timing, offscreen,
  boss exclusion, dynamic registration).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — remove the fixed Level 1 Wave 1 asteroid group.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — add a pure `globalWaveIndex` accessor (or
  equivalent) so the planner can key escalation to campaign progress.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` — update the Level 1 Wave 1 asteroid
  assertion.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — verify velocity injection path (no behaviour
  change expected).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` —
  document the new spawn mechanic.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** escalation is keyed to the cumulative global wave index
  across the campaign (not per-level resets), and the 13-wave shipped campaign
  reaches count 4 within a normal run.
- **Assumption:** "random edge" = uniform over the four screen edges; offscreen
  margin is a tunable constant (`half-size + small margin`).
- **Risk — wave stalls / asteroid accumulation:** more asteroids (plus large
  split chains = up to 7 kills each) can slow wave clearing, and asteroids
  survive timeouts and carry over, so their number can grow across waves.
  *Mitigation:* keep speeds slow, document tuning constants, and flag a
  possible concurrency cap / carry-over limit as a follow-up work item if
  playtesting shows a stall.
- **Risk — shallow inward velocity** could let an asteroid wrap before
  entering; *mitigation:* bias the velocity perpendicular to the spawn edge
  and clamp the angular spread.
- **Risk — non-determinism in tests:** *mitigation:* inject `rng` everywhere.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a concurrency cap, per-level resets, or UI for tuning
  are **out of scope** here; record any such opportunities as separate linked
  work items rather than expanding this item.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F** — Asteroids as an enemy (parent epic); established
  the entity, splitting, and wave integration.
- **AH-0MU8FORFF005RD9M** — PlayScene integration for asteroids.
- **AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L** — Asteroids survive wave timeout and carry over.
- **AH-0MUCG5TUG006I7X1** — Destroy carried-over asteroids on boss entry.
- **AH-0MUCG5T7S001F9MQ** — Keep asteroids moving/collidable during
  transitions.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1.2 (Asteroid design) and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1 (E6 Asteroid), §4.2 (wave structures).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Weight scheduling and count progression:** "How should the large-weight
  increase work per step, and does count double (2→4→8) or increment
  (2→4→6)?" — **Answer (operator):** "as recommended". Accepted answer
  (recommended option): baseline medium:large = 80:20; increase large weight by
  +20 each wave (medium fixed at 80); when large reaches 2× medium (160:80),
  reset to 80:20 and double the per-wave count (2→4→8). Source: interactive
  reply.
- **Q2 — Timing distribution for 4+ asteroids:** "For N asteroids per wave, how
  should spawn times distribute across the 30 s window?" — **Answer
  (operator):** "as recommended". Accepted answer (recommended option): first
  within 0–10 % of the wave timer; remaining N−1 distributed at ~equal
  intervals with ±5 % jitter so the mid-wave one lands near 50 %. Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Existing fixed asteroid group:** "Should the current
  `group('asteroid','single',1)` in Level 1 Wave 1 be removed, with all
  asteroids now handled by the new random spawner?" — **Answer (operator):**
  "as recommended". Accepted answer: yes — replace entirely and update existing
  tests. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 — Scope of spawns:** "Should asteroids appear in every wave of every
  level?" — **Answer (operator):** "every wave of every level". Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Q5 — Starting count and weighting:** spawn 2 per wave by default, weighted
  toward medium, escalating large weight with resets and count doubling. —
  **Answer (operator):** supplied in the same reply as Q4. Source: interactive
  reply.
- **Q6 — Spawn edge:** "Which edge and position?" — **Answer (operator):**
  "random". Accepted answer: uniform random edge with inward drift. Source:
  interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

# Hold-full Power-up Choice Dialog — Opaque Backdrop

## Problem Statement

The `MineralChoiceScene` overlay (shown when the ship's mineral hold fills and the player must choose a power-up) currently uses a translucent black backdrop (`alpha: 0.75`), allowing the paused game field to remain visible behind the dialog. The requirement is for the backdrop to be fully opaque, blanking out the entire screen behind the choice dialog.

## Users

- **Player** — When the hold fills, the choice dialog should be clearly visually separated from the gameplay field by a fully black screen, improving focus on the choice options.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Opaque backdrop** — The `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA` constant in `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` is set to `1.0` (fully opaque), replacing the current value of `0.75`.
2. **Visual result** — When `MineralChoiceScene` is displayed, the entire screen behind the choice options is solid black (no transparency).
3. **No visual regressions** — The power-up choice text and option labels remain clearly readable and unchanged in appearance.
4. **All tests pass** — The full project test suite passes, including `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`.

## Constraints

- This is a minimal, surgical change: only the backdrop alpha value is modified.
- No API changes, no new parameters, no behavioural changes to choice selection logic.
- The fix applies to both the main game (`PlayScene` → `MineralChoiceScene`) and the gym scenes where the choice overlay may be launched.

## Existing State

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` defines `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA = 0.75` on line ~40.
- The backdrop is drawn as a full-screen black rectangle: `this.add.rectangle(0, 0, GAME_WIDTH, GAME_HEIGHT, 0x000000, CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA)`.
- The comment above the constant describes it as "Translucent backdrop so the paused field remains visible behind."

## Desired Change

- Set `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA` to `1.0`.
- Update the comment to reflect the opaque/blanked-out behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — Change `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA` from `0.75` to `1.0` and update its comment.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — Verify existing tests pass (no test changes expected; the backdrop alpha is not directly tested).

## Related Work

- **AH-0MUCST52T003AX4V** — "Choice modal scene and PlayScene mineral wiring" (parent feature that created this scene).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — "Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship's hold and grant a power-up choice" (epic that introduced the hold-full mechanic).
- **AH-0MUCST2VY004T6QQ** — "Test: Hold-full choice scene and PlayScene wiring" (tests for the choice scene).
- **AH-0MUCST5W9009BH34** — "Documentation and full project test suite validation" (test validation).

# Tests: CSV codec (parse, serialise, coerce, validate)

Create the test suite for the CSV codec module (`src/core/csv.ts`) before implementing the codec itself.

**Context:**

The CSV codec module provides an RFC 4180 CSV parser and serializer that reads flat CSV rows into typed `EnemyConfig` / `ShipConfig` objects. This task creates the **tests** that define the expected behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CSV parsing — round-trip.** `parseCsvRows` accepts a CSV string (with header row) and returns an array of `Record<string, string>` objects. Each row produces one object; column names come from the header. Empty rows and comment lines (starting with `#`) are skipped.

2. **Type coercion.** `coerceEnemyConfig` converts raw string values to typed fields: numbers parsed via `Number(...)`, enums validated against `EnemyFormationKind` / `EnemyShotPattern`, colours coerced from `0xRRGGBB` hex strings, booleans coerced from `"true"` / `"false"`.

3. **Validation.** Missing required fields produce a validation error. Invalid enum values fall back to defaults. Malformed numbers fall back to `0`. Invalid hex colours fall back to `0x000000`. The validator returns a typed result with errors array (non-destructive).

4. **CSV serialization.** `serializeEnemyConfigs` converts typed `EnemyConfig` objects back to a CSV string with headers in a defined column order. Colours are formatted as `0xRRGGBB`. The output round-trips through `parseCsvRows` → `coerceEnemyConfig`.

5. **RFC 4180 quoting.** Values containing commas, double-quotes, or newlines are properly quoted (enclosed in `""`, with internal `"` escaped as `""`).

6. **Default fallbacks.** When a row has missing columns, `coerceEnemyConfig` fills in sensible defaults from `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` / `DEFAULT_CONFIG` — never returns `undefined` or `NaN`.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/csv.test.ts` — test suite for the codec (to be created).
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — type definitions for `EnemyConfig`, enums, and defaults.
- `src/core/config.ts` — type definitions for `ShipConfig` and defaults.

**Dependencies:**

- None (foundation task — must be implemented first).

**Deliverables:**

- `src/core/csv.test.ts` — comprehensive test suite covering all ACs above.
- (The codec implementation in `src/core/csv.ts` will be a separate task.)

# Tests: Config store (in-memory registry, boot load, dev write)

Create the test suite for the config store module (`src/core/configStore.ts`) before implementing the store itself.

**Context:**

The config store provides an in-memory registry that is populated at boot from the committed CSV files. It exposes synchronous `loadEnemyConfig` / `loadShipConfig` accessors. During development, it also supports writes via the Vite plugin endpoint and re-reads.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Boot load.** `loadConfigs()` fetches `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` and `src/data/ship-config.csv` (via HTTP fetch), parses and validates them, and populates the in-memory registry. The registry is ready before the first scene boots.

2. **Sync access.** `loadEnemyConfig(key)` returns the typed `EnemyConfig` from the registry synchronously. `loadShipConfig()` returns the `ShipConfig` synchronously. No async/await required by callers.

3. **Dev write + re-read.** In dev mode, `saveEnemyConfig(config)` writes via PUT to the Vite plugin endpoint, then re-reads the CSV and updates the registry. `saveShipConfig(config)` works the same way.

4. **Production fallback.** In production (static build), writes are disabled. `saveEnemyConfig` / `saveShipConfig` are no-ops that return a status indicating writes are unavailable. The registry is loaded from bundled CSV at build time.

5. **Graceful degradation.** If a CSV fetch fails at boot, the registry falls back to built-in defaults from `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` / `DEFAULT_CONFIG` without throwing. The game still boots.

6. **Key listing and all-configs.** `listEnemyConfigKeys()` and `loadAllEnemyConfigs()` serve from the registry, returning the same data shapes as the current implementation.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` — test suite (to be created).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — config store module (to be created).
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — type definitions and defaults.
- `src/core/config.ts` — type definitions and defaults.

**Dependencies:**

- None (foundation task — must be implemented first).

**Deliverables:**

- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` — comprehensive test suite covering all ACs above.

**Context:**

The config store (`src/core/configStore.ts`) replaces localStorage as the persistence layer. It fetches CSVs at boot, parses them using the CSV codec, and serves them synchronously. In dev mode, it supports writes via the Vite plugin endpoint.

# Tests: Vite CSV plugin (GET/PUT, atomic write, validation)

Create the test suite for the Vite CSV plugin before implementing the plugin itself.

**Context:**

The Vite plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`) exposes dev-server middleware endpoints for reading and writing CSV files. It runs only in dev mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **GET endpoint.** `GET /api/csv/src/data/enemy-configs.csv` returns the file contents with `Content-Type: text/csv`. The path is resolved relative to the project root.

2. **PUT endpoint (upsert).** `PUT /api/csv/src/data/enemy-configs.csv` with a CSV body validates the row, finds the matching key, and overwrites that row. The file is written atomically (temp file + rename).

3. **PUT endpoint (append for Save As).** `PUT` with a new key appends a new row. Duplicate keys are rejected with a 409 status.

4. **Validation.** Invalid CSV rows are rejected with a 400 status and a human-readable error message. The file is not modified on validation failure.

5. **Dev-only.** The plugin only registers when `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` or `import.meta.env.DEV` is true. In production builds, it is a no-op.

6. **Atomic write.** The file is written via a temp file in the same directory, then renamed. If the write fails mid-way, the original file is untouched.

**Key Files:**

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — test suite (to be created).
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — plugin module (to be created).

**Dependencies:**

- None for test file creation. Plugin implementation is a sibling task.

**Deliverables:**

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — comprehensive test suite covering all ACs above.

# Vite CSV plugin: dev middleware (GET/PUT, atomic write, validation)

Implement the Vite dev-server middleware plugin that exposes CSV read/write endpoints.

**Context:**

The plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`) registers GET and PUT handlers during development. It uses the CSV codec for validation and performs atomic writes via temp file + rename.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **GET handler.** Serves CSV files from `src/data/` with correct `Content-Type: text/csv`. Returns 404 for unknown paths.

2. **PUT handler — upsert.** Receives a CSV body, parses and validates it, finds the matching row by key, and overwrites it. Returns 200 with the updated row data.

3. **PUT handler — append (Save As).** When the key does not exist, appends a new row. Returns 201 (created) with the new row data.

4. **Validation errors.** Returns 400 with a JSON error object describing which fields are invalid. The file is not modified.

5. **Duplicate key rejection.** Returns 409 (Conflict) if Save As attempts to add a row with an existing key.

6. **Atomic write.** Uses `fs.writeFileSync` to a temp file (e.g., `.tmp_{filename}`), then `fs.renameSync` to replace the original. If rename fails, the original file is preserved.

7. **Dev-only registration.** The plugin only registers its middleware when Vite is running in dev mode (`server.mode === 'development'`).

8. **Registered in vite.config.ts.** The plugin is imported and added to the `plugins` array in `vite.config.ts`.

**Key Files:**

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — new plugin module (to be created).
- `./vite.config.ts` — updated to register the plugin.

**Deliverables:**

# CSV codec: RFC 4180 parser, serialiser, typed coercion, validation

Implement the CSV codec module (`src/core/csv.ts`) that parses flat CSV rows into typed `EnemyConfig` / `ShipConfig` objects and serialises them back.

**Context:**

The codec is the foundation of the CSV-based configuration system. It is used by the boot loader (to parse committed CSVs), the Vite plugin (to validate writes), and the config store (to re-read after writes). It must be dependency-free and hand-rolled (no new runtime dependencies).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parser.** `parseCsvRows(csv: string): Record<string, string>[]` parses an RFC 4180 CSV string with a header row into an array of objects. Empty rows and comment lines (starting with `#`) are skipped. A leading BOM (U+FEFF) is stripped.

2. **Serialiser.** `serializeEnemyConfigs(configs: EnemyConfig[]): string` and `serializeShipConfig(config: ShipConfig): string` produce a CSV string with a header row and one row per config. Output round-trips through `parseCsvRows` → coercion. Colours are formatted as `0xRRGGBB`.

3. **RFC 4180 quoting.** Fields containing commas, double-quotes, or newlines are wrapped in double quotes, with internal quotes escaped as `""`. The parser reverses this correctly.

4. **Typed coercion.** `coerceEnemyConfig(row, defaults)` and `coerceShipConfig(row, defaults)` convert raw string values to typed fields: numbers via `Number(...)`, enums validated against `EnemyFormationKind` / `EnemyShotPattern` / `ControlScheme`, colours via `parseInt(value, 16)`.

5. **Validation.** A validator returns a typed result `{ ok: boolean; errors: string[] }`. Missing required fields, malformed numbers, invalid enums, and invalid hex colours are reported. Coercion falls back to `defaults` for every invalid field — never produces `undefined`, `NaN`, or an invalid enum.

6. **Column mapping.** A documented, stable column order per config type (exported as constants) maps CSV headers to typed fields. Unknown headers are ignored; missing headers fall back to defaults.

7. **No runtime dependencies.** The codec uses only the TypeScript/JavaScript standard library.

**Key Files:**

# Ship config controlScheme does not survive game server restart

## Problem statement

Saving the player ship's control scheme (e.g. **Asteroids**) from the Player gym scene writes the value to `src/data/ship-config.csv`, but restarting the game server (`npm run dev`) loads the built-in default (`fourDirectional`) instead of the persisted value, because the boot loader that reads the CSV is never actually invoked in the runtime path.

## Users

Developer/designer tuning the player ship in the gym, who expects a saved value to be the single source of truth across sessions.

- As a designer, I want to save `controlScheme=asteroids` in the Player gym and have it still be asteroids after restarting `npm run dev`, so that I do not have to re-apply my tuning every session.
- As a developer, I want the CSV documented as "read at boot" to actually be read at boot, so the documented persistence contract holds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — On application boot (dev and production), the config store is hydrated from the persisted CSV **before** any scene reads `loadShipConfig()` / `loadEnemyConfig()`. Verify: after saving `controlScheme=asteroids` in the Player gym and restarting `npm run dev`, the Player gym boots in Asteroids mode and `loadShipConfig().controlScheme === 'asteroids'`.
- **AC2** — A regression test fails against the current code and passes after the fix: it asserts the runtime boot path calls `loadConfigs()` (or the store is otherwise hydrated from CSV) before the first scene consumes the config; `loadShipConfig()` then reflects the CSV value rather than `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.
- **AC3** — Editing `src/data/ship-config.csv` by hand and restarting `npm run dev` yields the edited values (matches README "Configuration (CSV)" §Boot / §Editing by hand).
- **AC4** — Failure fallback is preserved: if the CSV fetch/read fails, the game still boots with built-in defaults and does not throw.
- **AC5** — A testing/validation criterion: automated tests cover the boot-hydration path (success and failure) and run in `npm test`.
- **AC6** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No `localStorage` for config values — the committed CSV remains the single source of truth.
- `loadShipConfig()` / `loadEnemyConfig()` must remain **synchronous** for scene callers.
- `loadConfigs()` must never throw — a failed fetch falls back to built-in defaults so the game still boots.
- Production/static builds remain read-only (write path is dev-only and unchanged).
- Boot hydration must complete before scene construction so the first frame is correct (no flash of default scheme).

## Existing state

- `src/core/configStore.ts` defines `loadConfigs()` which fetches both CSVs (dev) or reads the bundled CSVs (production) and populates the in-memory registry.
- `loadConfigs()` is currently referenced only by the config-store tests (`configStore.test.ts`, `configStore.integration.test.ts`) — **it is never called from the runtime boot path** (`src/main.ts`, `src/core/Game.ts`, `src/core/gameConfig.ts`).
- `getRegistry()` lazily creates an empty registry whose `ship` is `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (`controlScheme: 'fourDirectional'`), so before `loadConfigs()` runs, `loadShipConfig()` returns the default.
- Saving from the gym (`GymPlayer._onSave` → `saveShipConfig`) writes the CSV **and updates the in-memory registry**, which is why the change works within the session but is lost on restart.
- The Vite dev-server plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`) writes the CSV atomically and the file on disk does contain the saved value (`git status` shows `M src/data/ship-config.csv`).
- README "Configuration (CSV)" documents that the store "reads both CSVs ... at startup" and that "edit a cell ... refresh `npm run dev` — the new values are live" — the documented contract is not met.

## Desired change

Wire the existing `loadConfigs()` into the application boot sequence so the CSV-backed registry is populated before the Phaser game and its scenes are constructed. The minimal fix is to make the entry point asynchronous: `await loadConfigs()` in `src/main.ts` before `new Game()` (or an equivalent async boot wrapper around `Game`), preserving the documented default-fallback behaviour.

Secondary (out of scope, tracked separately): the dev write path strips the `#` comment header from `src/data/ship-config.csv` on save, losing the human-readable column documentation. Reported as a discovered item, not part of this fix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/main.ts` — Entry point; hydrate the config store (`await loadConfigs()`) before constructing `Game`.
- `src/core/Game.ts` — May need an async boot hook/wrapper if hydration is owned here instead of `main.ts`.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — Builds the Phaser config; ensure hydration precedes scene registration/start.
- `src/core/config.ts` — Re-export `loadConfigs` if the entry point consumes the public config facade.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — Existing `loadConfigs()`; confirm idempotence and non-throwing fallback remain intact.
- `src/main.test.ts` (new) or `src/core/Game.boot.test.ts` (new) — Regression test asserting boot hydration ordering.
- `README.md` — "Configuration (CSV)" section: confirm/adjust boot wording once the path is real.

## Related work

- `AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD` — Alternative player control (introduced `controlScheme` + persistence; completed).
- `AH-0MTFRQR41000V57V` — Scheme-aware input routing in gym scenes (completed).
- `AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ` — Scheme-aware input tests for affected gym scenes (completed).
- `AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC` — Player cannot be moved in enemy and power-up gym scenes (consumes saved `controlScheme`; completed).
- `AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA` — Create a CSV file to maintain enemy configurations (parent epic, open).
- `AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9` — CSV seed data files (parent task, open).
- `AH-0MUE2MGZM0016U3L` — Config store: in-memory registry, boot load, dev write (blocked; the "boot load" half is the deliverable this bug affects).
- `README.md` — "Configuration (CSV)" (`src/data/ship-config.csv`, boot contract, dev write path).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — ship movement/control scheme tuning.

### Automated related-work report

- **AH-0MTHG5K6O008BCNJ** – Docs and README for enemy config pipeline (completed)
- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** – Add a Magnet power up (completed)
- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** – Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD (completed)

Repository file matches: `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (matched terms: config, csv, boot/loads, ship, scheme, save, restart, vite, plugin).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the only reason the restart loses the value is the missing `loadConfigs()` call; verified by grep (no runtime references) and the symptom match (in-session save updates the registry, restart does not).
- **Risk — boot sequencing:** adding `await` before game construction must not delay first paint unacceptably or break existing boot tests; mitigate by keeping the fetch fast and falling back to defaults without throwing.
- **Risk — test environment:** happy-dom/vitest do not have a real dev server; tests must mock `fetch` (the existing config-store tests already do this) — cover the boot path with the same seam.
- **Risk — scope creep:** comment-header stripping, and CSV edits not being live without a restart, are adjacent defects. Recorded as discovered items rather than folded into this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** What exactly do you mean by "restart of the game server" — (a) stop/start `npm run dev`, (b) `npm run build && npm run preview`, (c) something else?
  **Answer (operator):** (a) stop/start `npm run dev`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** When you say "That works" — does the Save button show a "Saved" confirmation, or "Save failed"?
  **Answer (operator):** confirmation. Source: interactive reply. Evidence: `GymPlayer._onSave` shows `Saved` when `saveShipConfig()` returns `ok: true`, which requires the dev PUT to succeed.
- **Q:** After the restart, does the ship default back to `fourDirectional`, or show some other unexpected behaviour?
  **Answer (operator):** back to default. Source: interactive reply.
- **Research summary:** `loadConfigs()` exists and is tested but is never invoked by `src/main.ts` / `src/core/Game.ts` / `src/core/gameConfig.ts`; `getRegistry()` falls back to `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (`fourDirectional`), so restart reverts to the default. The persisted CSV on disk does contain `asteroids`, confirming the write path works and the read path is the defect.

**Why it matters:** the committed CSVs are documented as the "single, human-editable source of truth" (README "Configuration (CSV)"). After the first gym save, the human-readable column documentation is lost, making the file harder to hand-edit.

**Suggested approach:** have the dev-server plugin preserve the original comment prefix when rewriting the file, or move the column documentation out of the CSV (e.g. README/schema) so it is not destroyed by writes.

# Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme and accept headerless CSV seed format

## Problem statement

The Player gym `Save` writes `src/data/ship-config.csv` through the dev-server CSV plugin in a **headerless** form (no leading `#` comment block, no trailing newline) and with `controlScheme=asteroids`. The committed built-in `DEFAULT_CONFIG.controlScheme` is `fourDirectional`, so the seed tests fail:

- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — header-comment assertion, `controlScheme` default mismatch, trailing-newline assertion.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — AC5 production fallback (`loadShipConfig()` no longer equals `DEFAULT_CONFIG`).

**Producer decision (2026-09-24):** Asteroids is the intended default control scheme, and the seed-file tests must no longer require the CSV comment header or a trailing newline. This supersedes acceptance criterion **AC5 (comment header)** of *CSV seed data files (`AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9`)* and retires the premise of the open bug *Gym config save strips the CSV comment header block (`AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4`)*.

## User story

As a game designer, I want the player ship to default to the **Asteroids** control scheme and the CSV seed files to be allowed to use the headerless format produced by the gym Save, so that the committed default matches my saved tuning and the seed tests no longer block gym saves.

## Expected behaviour

- `DEFAULT_CONFIG.controlScheme === 'asteroids'` (built-in fallback used when the CSV cannot be read).
- The committed `src/data/ship-config.csv` holds a single ship row with `controlScheme=asteroids` (gym-saved format).
- The seed tests for `ship-config.csv` no longer assert a leading `#` comment header or a trailing newline; all remaining assertions pass.
- The full suite passes; the build passes.

## Scope

In scope:

- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — default control scheme.
- `src/data/ship-config.csv` — committed seed value.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — drop the ship-config header/trailing-newline requirements.
- Any other test that hard-codes the old default and must follow the new one.

Out of scope:

- Changing the dev-server write path (comment-header stripping) — behaviour is now accepted.
- Changing `enemy-configs.csv` or its tests (left intact).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Default scheme.** `DEFAULT_CONFIG.controlScheme === 'asteroids'` in `src/core/configDefaults.ts`. Verify: unit/seed test assertion via `coerceShipConfig`.
2. **Seed CSV.** `src/data/ship-config.csv` contains exactly one ship row with all fields matching `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, including `controlScheme=asteroids`, and parses via the CSV codec.

4. **Suite green.** `npm test` passes in full (no failures).
5. **Documentation.** `README.md` (Configuration (CSV)) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§8.2) describe the headerless `ship-config.csv` format and that the `#` comment header is optional and not preserved by the gym Save.

# Allow `v*` release tags to deploy to the `github-pages` environment (reproducible policy + docs)

## Problem statement

`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` triggers on `v*` tag pushes, but the repository's `github-pages` environment has a custom deployment branch policy that allows only the `dev` branch. Every release tag is therefore rejected by environment protection, so the Pages deploy fails, the failed check run lands on the release-branch HEAD, and the ship release wrapper's `waitForPRMerge()` always falls back to a manual merge.

## Users

- **Operator (release runner):** runs the ship release and expects it to auto-merge and publish without the manual-merge fallback.
- **Player:** expects each release to be live and playable at `https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/`.
- **Future maintainer:** sets up or recovers the repository and needs a reproducible, documented way to configure the Pages environment policy.

### Example user stories

- As a release runner, I want pushing a `v*` release tag to deploy to GitHub Pages without environment-protection rejection, so that the release PR's checks pass and the ship wrapper merges the PR automatically.
- As a future maintainer, I want a documented, idempotent script that configures the `github-pages` environment deployment policy, so I do not have to rediscover the `dev`-only policy failure.
- As a player, I want every release to be published automatically at the project Pages URL.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Tag policy present.** The `github-pages` environment has a deployment policy for tags matching `v*`, in addition to the existing `dev` branch policy. Verify: `gh api repos/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies --jq '.branch_policies[] | "\(.type):\(.name)"'` outputs both `branch:dev` and `tag:v*`.
- **Reproducible, idempotent setup script.** `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` exists, is executable, adds the `v*` tag policy only when missing, and is safe to re-run (second run makes no change and exits 0). It fails loudly with a clear message when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated. Verify: `bash -n` syntax check plus running it twice and inspecting the API result.
- **Deploy succeeds end to end.** Re-running workflow run `35993333739` (tag `v0.1.5`) completes with both the `build` and `deploy` jobs `success`, and `https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/` serves the game. Verify: `gh run view 35993333739 --json conclusion,jobs` and an HTTP request to the Pages URL.
- **Tag-only trigger preserved.** `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes; non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy. Verify: workflow YAML inspected and unchanged.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Only a `v*` tag policy may be added; the existing `dev` branch policy must be preserved.
- The workflow's tag-only trigger semantics must not change (superseding Github Hosted Alpha (`AH-0MU9P20Q2003D2V0`) AC5 is out of scope).
- The fix must live in this repository plus the GitHub repository setting; the global ship skill must not be edited (out of repository scope).
- Applying the setting requires a `gh` token with repository admin; if unavailable, the operator applies it manually and the script/documentation records the requirement.

## Existing state

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` triggers on `push` of tags matching `v*`; the `deploy` job targets environment `github-pages`.
- Environment `github-pages` has `custom_branch_policies: true` with exactly one policy: `branch:dev`. No tag policy exists.
- Release flow (`merge-dev-to-main.sh`) tags `vX.Y.Z` on the release merge commit, pushes the tag and the release branch, then opens the PR to `main`. The tag push triggers the deploy, whose rejection leaves a failed check on the release-branch HEAD, blocking `run-release.js`'s `waitForPRMerge()`.
- Evidence: workflow run `35993333739` (`event: push`, `headBranch: v0.1.5`) — `build` succeeded, `deploy` failed with zero steps (environment protection rejection).
- No `scripts/` directory exists and README has no deployment/Pages configuration section.

## Desired change

- Add a `tag:v*` deployment policy to the `github-pages` environment (keeping `branch:dev`).
- Add an idempotent, documented setup script that applies and verifies the policy via `gh api`.
- Document the environment policy requirement and the script in README.
- Verify by re-running the failed workflow run so the release tag deploys successfully.

## Key Files

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` — New idempotent script that adds/verifies the `v*` tag deployment policy on the `github-pages` environment via `gh api`.
- `README.md` — New deployment subsection documenting the `github-pages` environment policy requirement and script usage.
- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` — No change expected; tag-only trigger retained and verified.
- GitHub repository setting — `github-pages` environment deployment policy (applied by the script, verified via `gh api`).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The `gh` token has repository-admin rights to modify environment policies; otherwise the operator applies the policy manually and the script reports the required command.
- **Risk:** The environment protection rule is the sole cause of the failure. Mitigation: re-run the workflow and confirm `deploy` succeeds; inspect `gh api .../pages` if it still fails.
- **Risk:** `gh run rerun 35993333739` may be disallowed or the run may be too old. Mitigation: fall back to pushing a fresh `v*` tag through the normal release flow.
- **Risk:** Wildcard tag policy (`v*`) may not be accepted by the API. Mitigation: verify with a GET after POST and adjust the pattern if needed.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Hardening the ship wrapper to ignore non-required checks (the original Option C) is out of scope for this repository and would be a separate work item in the agent-framework repo.

## Related work

- Github Hosted Alpha (`AH-0MU9P20Q2003D2V0`) — completed feature that introduced the tag-triggered Pages workflow; its AC5 requires that non-tag events do not deploy.

## Summary

Test-first verifier feature for *GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev)* (`AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77`). Adds an automated regression test that pins the **tag-only trigger contract** of `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`, so a future workflow edit cannot silently start deploying on branch pushes or pull requests.

## User story

As a future maintainer, I want an automated test that fails if the Pages deploy workflow starts triggering on non-tag events, so the tag-only release contract is protected without manual YAML review.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criterion **AC4** requires that `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes, and that non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy.
- The workflow currently declares `on.push.tags: ['v*']` and a `deploy` job targeting environment `github-pages`.
- This item is created and completed **before** the environment-policy implementation items (test-first ordering).

## Scope

In scope:

- A hermetic vitest test that reads `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` from the repository root and asserts its trigger shape.

Out of scope:

- Changing the workflow (no change is expected for this fix).
- Calling the live GitHub API.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes; non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy.
- The test asserts the only trigger is `push` with `tags: ['v*']` — no `branches`, no `pull_request`, and no `workflow_dispatch`.
- The test asserts the workflow contains a `deploy` job targeting the `github-pages` environment and a `build` job the deploy needs.
- The test is hermetic (reads only the checked-out workflow file) and runs as part of `npm test` with no new runtime dependency (`npm run build` and `npm test` both pass).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a vitest test (e.g. `scripts/deploy-pages-workflow.test.ts`, or co-located under `src/` if `scripts/` has no test wiring) that reads the workflow file using `node:fs` relative to the repo root.
- Parse the workflow text with focused assertions (regex/string checks or `yaml` if already available transitively); avoid adding a production dependency for a single test.
- Assert: `push.tags` is exactly `['v*']`; no `push.branches`; no `pull_request` / `workflow_dispatch` trigger keys; `jobs.deploy.environment.name == 'github-pages'`.
- Confirm the test is picked up by the existing `vitest.config.ts` include globs; adjust the include pattern only if the file lives outside the current test roots.

## Deliverables

- New automated trigger-contract test.
- `npm test` green including the new test.

## Dependencies

None.

## Key Files

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` — The workflow whose trigger contract is asserted (no change expected).
- `vitest.config.ts` — Test include globs; may need to cover the new test location.
- `scripts/deploy-pages-workflow.test.ts` — New hermetic regression test.
